tests.name: test_three
tests.description: Countdown(3) gives 3, 2 and 1.
tests.message: The first values of Countdown(3) are [2, 1, 0], not [3, 2, 1].

tests.name: test_zero_and_one
tests.description: Countdown(0) and Countdown(-2) give nothing, and Countdown(1) gives 1.

tests.name: test_for_loop
tests.description: A for loop over Countdown(100) adds up to 5,050.
tests.message: A for loop over Countdown(100) added up to 4,950, not 5,050 = 100 + 99 + ... + 1.

tests.name: test_used_up
tests.description: An iterator is used up after one loop over it, and stays used up.
tests.message: The first loop over Countdown(4) gave [3, 2, 1, 0], not [4, 3, 2, 1].

tests.name: test_iter_is_self
tests.description: iter of a Countdown is the Countdown itself.

tests.name: test_example
tests.description: Lists and strings of different lengths take turns.

tests.name: test_no_streams
tests.description: With no streams, interleave gives nothing.

tests.name: test_one_pass_streams
tests.description: Generators, which can be read only once, take turns too.

tests.name: test_endless
tests.description: An endless stream goes on after the others are used up.

tests.name: test_none_is_a_value
tests.description: A stream that holds None is not taken to be used up.

tests.name: test_everything_once
tests.description: Every item of every stream comes out once, each stream's items in their order.

tests.name: test_example
tests.description: The three documents of the example make three lists of 4.

tests.name: test_leftovers_dropped
tests.description: Tokens too few to fill a list are dropped, end tokens included.
tests.message: pack([[1, 2, 3]], 3, 0) gave [[1, 2, 3], [0]], not [[1, 2, 3]]: the end token left over after it is too few to fill a list.

tests.name: test_long_documents
tests.description: A document longer than a list is split across lists.

tests.name: test_empty_documents
tests.description: An empty document still adds its end token.

tests.name: test_lengths_and_order
tests.description: Every list has `length` tokens, and the lists, end to end, are the start of the stream of tokens.
tests.message: With length 2, pack gave the list [-1], whose length is 1.

tests.name: test_new_lists
tests.description: Each list handed out is a list of its own, which later tokens never change.

tests.name: test_endless_stream
tests.description: pack works on an endless stream of documents, taking each document only when it needs its tokens.

tests.name: test_train
tests.description: Three epochs over train.txt each see its 4 examples.

tests.name: test_other_files
tests.description: Every epoch sees every line, for files of 0, 1 and 7 lines and 1, 2 and 5 epochs.
tests.message: With a file of 1 line and 2 epochs, seen_per_epoch gave [1, 0], not [1, 1].

tests.name: test_no_epochs
tests.description: Zero epochs give an empty list.

tests.name: test_streams_each_epoch
tests.description: Each epoch opens the file afresh, rather than carrying on from a stream or a list made earlier.
tests.message: Over three epochs, seen_per_epoch opened train.txt once, not once in each epoch: each epoch should open the file afresh, rather than carry on from a stream or a list made earlier.

tests.name: test_one_line_at_a_time
tests.description: Each epoch counts the lines as they stream past, never holding all of them at once.
